construct: In systemic tissues, carbon dioxide enters erythrocytes and is rapidly converted by carbonic anhydrase to bicarbonate and hydrogen ions. Bicarbonate leaves the erythrocyte in exchange for chloride through the HCO3-/Cl- exchanger, allowing most carbon dioxide to be transported in plasma as bicarbonate while maintaining electroneutrality.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: In systemic capillaries, CO2-derived bicarbonate exits RBCs in exchange for chloride through band 3/AE1; the direction reverses in the lung.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Bicarbonate entry/chloride exit is physiologically real in pulmonary capillaries, but the stem explicitly locates the process in metabolically active systemic tissue.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Tissue location and plasma bicarbonate carriage uniquely fix the exchange direction.
